meta.scene_summary: We are busy building robot APIs while the actual infrastructure is busy going bankrupt or getting hacked.

cooking.headline: Rust finds a bug hiding in the borrow checker for 11 years
cooking.summary: Rust developers pride themselves on memory safety, but it turns out a bug has been quietly living in the borrow checker since before most of us even knew the language. It's the coding equivalent of finding out your 'unbreakable' security door had a spare key under the mat for over a decade.
cooking.plain_english: A technical flaw has been identified in the Rust programming language's memory safety system that has existed for eleven years.

cooking.headline: Physical Intelligence just dropped the API for your robot uprising
cooking.summary: We've finally reached the point where you can import a library to make your toaster do parkour. It's all fun and games until your Roomba decides it's too good for the kitchen floor and starts debugging your living room setup.
cooking.plain_english: A company has released a software interface that allows developers to integrate advanced artificial intelligence into various types of robotic hardware.

cooking.headline: Topgolf realized that paying VMware is a great way to lose $11 million
cooking.summary: Topgolf saved a small fortune by moving away from VMware, proving that sometimes the best way to optimize your budget is just to leave the building. It turns out the most expensive part of your infrastructure is often the license key itself.
cooking.plain_english: Topgolf saved over $11 million by switching from VMware virtualization software to a different platform.

cooking.headline: Google just dropped Gemini 4 Argon, because apparently, we needed a new model this week.
cooking.summary: Google is back with another model release, proving that the shelf life of a 'state-of-the-art' AI is currently shorter than a carton of milk. It's the tech equivalent of a group project where the deadline keeps moving forward, and everyone is just trying to keep up.
cooking.plain_english: Google has released Gemini 4 Argon, which is the latest iteration of their artificial intelligence model.

cooked.headline: Character.ai files for bankruptcy, proving even AI boyfriends have financial problems
cooked.summary: The startup promised us infinite digital companions, but apparently, they couldn't generate enough revenue to keep the lights on. It turns out that even the most advanced chatbots can't help you with the one thing that actually matters: basic accounting.
cooked.plain_english: Character.ai has filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy to restructure its business while continuing operations.

cooked.headline: The Dutch government decided they'd rather debug open source than pay for Microsoft 365
cooked.summary: The Dutch tax authorities looked at their Microsoft cloud migration and decided the privacy risks were essentially a subscription to a bad time. It turns out that when your day job is auditing people, you eventually develop an allergy to opaque black-box software.
cooked.plain_english: The Dutch tax agency has stopped its plan to use Microsoft 365 services due to data privacy concerns and will switch to open-source alternatives instead.

cooked.headline: OpenAI really took 'building in public' to a creepy new level
cooked.summary: An OpenAI engineer allegedly tried to bug an executive conference room, proving that internal corporate espionage is the new office politics. Apparently, they really wanted to know if the secret to AGI is just better meeting notes or something slightly more illegal.
cooked.plain_english: An employee at OpenAI was arrested after being accused of recording private conversations inside a conference room used by company executives.

cooked.headline: A cyberattack just hit the pause button on an entire underwater tunnel
cooked.summary: Building a massive tunnel between two countries is hard enough without someone deciding to execute a remote kill switch on the construction site. It turns out that even multi-billion dollar infrastructure projects are no match for a classic 'did you try turning it off and on again' security vulnerability.
cooked.plain_english: A digital security breach has forced the temporary suspension of construction work on a major tunnel project connecting Denmark and Germany.

cooked.headline: Hardware wallets that come with a free, unsolicited cellular data plan
cooked.summary: Thieves are shipping modified crypto wallets that include an eSIM to broadcast your private keys to the world. It's the hardware equivalent of buying a locked room only to find out the walls are made of glass.
cooked.plain_english: Hackers are selling tampered hardware cryptocurrency wallets that use a secret cellular connection to steal user funds.

cooked.headline: The Grace Hopper Celebration just cancelled, and the irony is palpable.
cooked.summary: The world's largest gathering for women in tech just pulled the plug on their main event. It's like throwing a massive party for diversity and inclusion, only to realize you forgot to send the invites to the actual attendees.
cooked.plain_english: The AnitaB.org organization has cancelled the Grace Hopper Celebration, which was a major annual conference for women in the technology industry.
